Homologous Chromosomes
Each cell of an organism produced by sexual reproduction has 2 copies of each autosome 
One copy received from each parent 
The 2 copies known as homologous chromosomes (homologues) 
Same size, shape, carry same genes for same traits
explanation: In organisms produced by sexual reproduction, each cell contains two copies of each autosome, with one copy inherited from each parent. These pair of matching chromosomes are known as homologous chromosomes, or homologues. Homologous chromosomes share the same size, shape, and carry genes that control the same biological traits.

opts: Chromosomes that are completely different in size and shape
Two copies of an autosome that have the same size, shape, and carry the same genes for the same traits
Replicated chromatids joined by a centromere
questions.exp: Homologous chromosomes (homologues) are two copies of an autosome (one from each parent) that are the same size, shape, and carry the same genes for the same traits.
